Filmmaker Sean Dunne joins Danny Jones to talk about a road film through the American fringe. The episode title calls it a psychedelic trip through the American wasteland. Dunne is known for short films on odd corners of US life.

Dunne tells how he finds his subjects and earns the trust of people who live far off the grid. He talks about drugs, faith, and the look of a land left behind. Jones draws out the tales from his shoots that stayed with him. Listeners get a film maker's tour of the strange heart of the country. The library files the talk as an archive record.

Filmmaker Oliver Stone and historian Peter Kuznick join Tucker Carlson for a talk on war and who gains from it. The title names war profits, nuclear tech, NATO and Russia, and war with Iran. Both guests have spent years on these themes.

Stone and Kuznick argue that arms firms and their allies push the country toward war. They warn that nuclear risk grows as talks with Russia and Iran fail. Carlson draws out their view of NATO and the path to peace. Listeners get the anti-war case from two of its best known voices. The talk is long, sharp, and full of history.
